allowed_claim: Ordinary/utility CPU state modulates the measured Gutenberg input path; background/maintenance CPU does not.
current_evidence: Near-key no-CPU controls stay slow at median p50 24.3ms, continuous ordinary/utility CPU is fast at 9.7ms, and background/maintenance CPU is slow at 24.2ms.
blocked_overclaim: Naming P-core residency, frequency, cache, scheduler QoS, or Chromium scheduler state from aggregate p50 rows.
required_next_evidence: None for the boundary claim; a sidecar plus privileged counters for the named mechanism.

allowed_claim: A nearby no-op callback, delayed task, IPC command, idle child, or worker lifetime is not sufficient.
current_evidence: Six near-key no-CPU controls remain slow, with p50 range 22.2-24.6ms.
blocked_overclaim: Explaining the fast band as merely a callback existing before the key.
required_next_evidence: No more no-CPU rows unless a concrete new browser subsystem is targeted.

allowed_claim: Generic external CPU activity is not sufficient; the effect is policy-sensitive.
current_evidence: Background and maintenance QoS CPU controls consume CPU but remain slow at median p50 24.2ms.
blocked_overclaim: Claiming that any load, any process activity, or any warm CPU is enough.
required_next_evidence: Privileged counters only to identify the lower-level policy or hardware state.

allowed_claim: Finite CPU work has a descriptive duration and recency relationship with the next retained key.
current_evidence: The two-variable finite-burst model has R^2 = 0.71 with expected coefficient signs.
blocked_overclaim: Treating the regression as proof of frequency, scheduler, cache, or browser queue state.
required_next_evidence: Join finite rows to per-key frequency/residency, scheduler, wakeup, and browser-task counters.

current_evidence: Ordinary/utility versus background/maintenance policy split is consistent with a power or residency boundary, but current artifacts do not contain residency/frequency counters.
blocked_overclaim: Claiming P-core, cluster, frequency, or power-state causality from browser timing alone.
required_next_evidence: Sidecar dry run, then root powermetrics joined to retained key windows.

current_evidence: The split tracks ordinary/utility versus background/maintenance policy more closely than Unix nice or taskpolicy latency/throughput tiers.
blocked_overclaim: Claiming scheduler or QoS placement without runnable latency, wakeup, core-selection, and effective-QoS records.
required_next_evidence: Root trace only after powermetrics cannot explain the split.

allowed_claim: Fallback candidate only after OS scheduler and power-state counters are insufficient.
current_evidence: Gutenberg's broad JS/data/RichText path could be memory-sensitive, but external child CPU controls mean the mechanism cannot require warming Gutenberg objects directly.
blocked_overclaim: Claiming cache or memory causality from the local JS timing shape.
required_next_evidence: Lower-level renderer counters joined to retained EventDispatch windows after OS and browser scheduling are controlled.

allowed_claim: Open only after OS counters fail to explain the split.
current_evidence: Runtime-protocol and CPU/QoS controls show a browser/runtime boundary below Gutenberg source spans, but the current CPU/QoS rows do not include scheduler trace categories.
blocked_overclaim: Naming V8, browser task queue, or scheduler state before OS power/QoS state is matched.
required_next_evidence: Trace-off protocol sidecar first; scheduler/task-queue categories after OS counter alignment.

allowed_claim: Keep product mitigation separate from system-mechanism naming.
current_evidence: Native controls move less than 1ms while Gutenberg moves by many milliseconds; Gutenberg fanout supplies the scale.
blocked_overclaim: Treating a system-state mechanism as a source-level fix, or treating source fanout as proof of the system mechanism.
required_next_evidence: Selector/subscriber prototypes and workload replay for product lag; OS counters for the benchmark artifact.

allowed_claim: Do not name the exact mechanism until one recorded state predicts all discriminating rows.
current_evidence: The compact rows and join contract are selected, but the joined per-key counter table does not exist yet.
blocked_overclaim: Updating the report from class medians, one successful row family, or unrelated explanations for separate row families.
required_next_evidence: Joined per-key table covering no-CPU slow, ordinary/utility fast, background/maintenance slow, finite fresh/stale, and observer controls.
